evidence: src/enrolments/enrolments.controller.ts: @Controller('enrolments') and @Post() / @Post('withdrawals') come from @nestjs/common and are routing decorators, which belong in the presentation layer
enrol(@Body() dto: EnrolDto): Promise<Enrolment> passes the request straight to this.enrolmentsService.enrol(dto.courseId, dto.studentEmail), which is application-layer orchestration
withdraw(...) awaits enrolmentsService.withdraw(...) and returns { refund }. This only shapes the response; the refund decision is made in the service
constructor(private readonly enrolmentsService: EnrolmentsService) injects an application-layer service, which presentation may depend on
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The controller fits the presentation role. It uses NestJS routing decorators (@Controller, @Post, @Body), which belong in the presentation layer. It receives an application DTO, sends all work to the injected application-layer EnrolmentsService, and returns either the domain Enrolment or a small response object. The constructor injects EnrolmentsService from the application layer, which presentation may depend on, so this is normal dependency wiring. The file has no business rule, invariant, calculation or decision: wrapping the `refund` boolean from the service in `{ refund }` only shapes the response. No candidate flags were raised.
